page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes. Page number at the head right. Running head at the head centre. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: lubres epulas perpetuò adnumerata eft, ficciorem enim agnina, efuiquè aptiorem effe communi conlenfu traditur,qnin & cætero-rum quadrupedum carnibus anteponitur: Hefiodus l.2. ωτ' ἐργων [?] &c. hoedorum primogenitorum carnem maximè commendat, vt boni fucci,facilisque coctionis. Gedeoné [?] hoedum caprarium coxiffe,angeloq;, quem inuitarat,in conuiuio appofuiffe, sacra monimenta teftantur. Sapiunt autem tunc maximè hoedi cum herbarum sunt expertes,bi-meftres,atque etiam trimeftres, si mater la-ctea-bundet,adultiores enim & ab vbere depulsi saporis suauitatsq; gratiam amittunt. Nullam autem aliam magis idoneam à morbo se recolligentibus quidam promittunt, quin etiam otio deditis, & non laborantibus salubriter editur, grauiores verò operas exercentibus insalubriter, facilè enim alimentum eius diffipatur atque euanescit. Galenus l.de fan.tuen. Senibus non incommodam spondet. Manditur elixa pariter atque tolta [?], & quidem recens. Cocta, quæ refrixerit,ca-lente cesetur vtilior Mauritanorum opinione. Galenus frigidam esse edendam voluit in commentario l.4.de rat.vict.in acutis. Quod Plutarchus prodidit de caprina,qui eam gustarint aut attigerint,comitiali morbo affici, auditur verius quam creditur. Caeterum praeclaram in medicinis laudem

page.notes: Printed page number reads 45ʒ, taken as 453. Several Greek and Latin words are doubtful and marked [?]: the Hesiod Greek opening, "Gedeoné", "tolta" and the Galen citation "l.de fan.tuen." (the first letters are unclear). Lines are joined across the printed line ends. The text runs over from the previous page and ends mid-sentence at the foot, with the catchword "ad" below.
